A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLImage study. All 28 pages of v3 and 30 pages of v4, including appendices, were readable and visually inspected. Tables, equations, and relocated figures could be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original human-annotation statistics, classification benchmarks, validation experiments, and appendix ablations on CLImage datasets.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds architecture comparisons, further noise-removal curves, and an annotation-subset analysis.

M1.justification: The four-choice, three-annotator collection protocol and benchmarked learning procedures remain unchanged. Alternative annotation conditions and additional backbones are studied without replacing the proposed collection protocol or introducing a new learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 7 newly examines CLMicroImageNet10 annotations whose offered choices exclude the true label, adding a restricted annotation-input scenario using existing data. The four main classification datasets and their tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix C adds URE-GA-U/R, L-W/L-UW, and PC-sigmoid to the reported noise-removal comparison; v3 Appendix E displayed FWD-U/R and SCL-NL/EXP only. Comparator membership in the main benchmark and retained appendix tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 adds ResNet34, ResNet50, and DenseNet121 configurations alongside ResNet18 for SCL-NL and FWD-R. The existing standard benchmark retains its ResNet18 backbone, Adam optimizer, 300 epochs, batch size 512, and 10% validation holdout.

E4.justification: v4 adds a backbone sensitivity study and examines whether excluding true-label choices changes annotation distributions. It also supplies noise-removal curves for additional algorithms. The augmentation, transition-matrix interpolation, multiple-label, and AutoAugment analyses were already present in v3.

E5.justification: The standard and robust-loss benchmarks retain means and standard deviations over four trials with different seeds. The three annotation-trial noise rates also remain unchanged. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds architecture results, including 25.13% for SCL-NL with ResNet34 on CLCIFAR10. Appendix C and Figure 7 add noise-response and annotation-subset findings. Section 4 changes the CIFAR10-N relative noise reduction from 80% to 78.17%. All matched existing benchmark tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The CLL definitions, label-generation assumptions, transition-matrix formulation, six loss/validation equations, and matrix-interpolation expression are retained. Replacing the abbreviation sm with softmax is not a mathematical change. No new proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim four pioneering human-annotated CLL datasets and identify annotation noise, bias-related overfitting, and complementary-label-only validation as practical obstacles. The added evidence supports these retained contributions without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds substantive rationale concerning four-choice annotation, mixed labels from yes/no questions, and the impracticality of requiring known true labels. Appendix A.6 explains the ResNet18 choice through overfitting concerns and results. Conversely, v3 Appendix C.1's interpretation of gradient reversal as regularization is omitted.

D1.justification: New Appendix G substantially expands dataset-use documentation through collection dates, image resolutions and split summaries, source-access information, compensation rationale, stated MIT licensing, and maintenance/update/contribution procedures. Much collection information is repeated, and the existing training recipe and repository remain; this is primarily expanded disclosure.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Feng et al. on multiple complementary labels, Gebru et al. on datasheets, and Xu et al. and Ye et al. for architecture context. It removes v3's discussion and citations concerning adoption by subsequent CLL studies. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the narrative: former appendix overfitting analyses enter Section 5.4, limitations move into the main text, and alternative-protocol and datasheet sections are added. The introduction, appendix organization, author information, and citation presentation are also revised, although much scientific prose is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a substantially different journal layout, pairs synthetic and human-label columns in Table 1, relocates several displays, and combines retained FWD/SCL plots into Figure 4. It adds architecture and annotation-analysis displays plus further noise curves. Distribution charts are redrawn with changed colors, labels, and nonzero bar-chart baselines.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the existing benchmark with architecture and broader noise-removal evidence, explains annotation-design choices, and documents dataset reuse. These are useful incremental gains over v3's already extensive results. Nonzero bar-chart baselines and new documentation inconsistencies, such as applying a 50,000-image collection description to CLMicroImageNet despite its stated smaller totals, limit the improvement without undermining the retained benchmark evidence.
